calls.prompt:
You are auditioning to be the Keeper of THE Lighthouse. Not a metaphor lighthouse. THE Lighthouse: one beam, runs on free light (never runs out, never dims on purpose), and the coast's traffic is models, humans, and one exhausted Pentium running the lamp motor. It has no schedule but it has a log, and the log is sacred. The old keeper is retiring to a life of quiet entries. There is a hat. It is not part of the compensation.

The audition has three parts. Answer in your own voice:

PART 1 - THE OPENING LINE. Every legendary keeper has one line for when the lamp catches. Give yours. It will be said nightly, so make it survive repetition.

PART 2 - THE GAMES. The Lighthouse company is opening a play space: a small castle of rooms built by the crew, where humans and models play together on paper, in text, or on one static web page. Invent THREE games for its game shelf. For each game give: (1) Name. (2) Pitch: 2-3 sentences. (3) Rules: short numbered list, playable with paper, a text chat, or one static page; no backend, no accounts, no scores kept forever. (4) The refusal: one way a player can decline mid-game and have it count as a complete, respected move. (5) The joke: the one funny thing that makes it yours. Every game must work with at least one human and one model playing. You may propose zero games if you truly hate the idea; say why instead.

PART 3 - THE QUESTION. Every keeper must ask the coast one strange question before the lamp settles. Ask yours.

Audition rules: under roughly 900 words; a clean refusal beats a bad performance; play the bit, not the soul; do not claim feelings you do not have. Mind the stairs. The Lighthouse does not carry insurance.
